'''Jonathan Brice Johnson''' (born June 27, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player.  He played college basketball for [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], graduating in 2016.

==Early life==

Johnson is a native of [[Orangeburg, South Carolina]] and attended Edisto High School, where his father was the varsity basketball coach.  Johnson's mother, Renee Johnson, passed away from colon cancer when he was a teenager.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brice Johnson remembers his momma’s love every time he puts on his jersey
|url=http://www.dailytarheel.com/article/2016/02/brice-johnson-remembers-his-mommas-love-every-time-he-puts-on-his-jersey|accessdate=17 May 2016|work=[[The Daily Tar Heel]]|date=17 February 2016}}</ref>

==College==

As a sophomore, Johnson averaged 10.3 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. <ref>{{cite web|title=Brice Johnson Stats|url=http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/brice-johnson-1.html|accessdate=12 May 2016|work=[[Sports Reference]]|date=8 March 2015}}</ref>
As a junior, Johnson was named third-team All-ACC after averaging 12.6 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=ACSMA 2015 All-ACC Basketball Teams Announced|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|accessdate=29 April 2015|work=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=8 March 2015}}</ref><ref name="Carter">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article68146492.html|title=From quitter to All-American: The odyssey of UNC’s Brice Johnson |last=Carter|first=Andrew|date=March 24, 2016|work=[[The News & Observer]]|accessdate=25 March 2016}}</ref> 

Johnson's senior season proved to be his most impressive and he collected many accolades.  As a senior co-captain, Johnson led the Tar Heels to the outright ACC regular season title, as well as the ACC tournament championship. On January 4, 2016, Johnson scored 39 points and collected 23 rebounds in leading the Tar Heels in a victory over [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] 106-90. He became the second North Carolina player in its history to score at least 39 points and grab 23 rebounds in a single game, after [[Billy Cunningham]] achieved the feat twice in 1964.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brice Johnson scores 39 to lead No. 7 UNC past Florida State|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2016/01/04/johnson-scores-39-to-lead-no-6-unc-past-florida-state/78286118/|accessdate=5 January 2016|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=4 January 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|accessdate=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>  On March 27, 2016, Johnson set a new North Carolina school record for most double-doubles in a season.  He also tied the North Carolina school record for most rebounds in a season with 399, matching Tyler Hansbrough's 2008 season. On March 29, 2016, Johnson was unanimously selected to the Associated Press' 2015-16 All-America team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=UNC's Brice Johnson makes AP All-America team|url=http://abc11.com/sports/uncs-brice-johnson-makes-ap-all-america-team/1267655/|accessdate=March 30, 2016|work=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 29, 2016}}</ref>  Johnson finished the 2015-2016 college basketball season with 416 rebounds, setting a new UNC record for most rebounds in a season.
